name: glm.diag.plots
title: Diagnostics plots for generalized linear models

origin.description: Draws jackknife deviance residuals against the linear predictor, a normal QQ plot of standardized deviance residuals, Cook statistics against leverage over one minus leverage, and Cook statistics against case number.
origin.usage:
glm.diag.plots(glmfit, glmdiag = glm.diag(glmfit), subset = NULL,
               iden = FALSE, labels = NULL, ret = FALSE)

arguments.name: glmfit
arguments.text: A glm object, the result of glm().

arguments.name: glmdiag
arguments.text: Diagnostics from glm.diag. Calculated if not supplied.

arguments.name: subset
arguments.text: Case numbers for the Cook plot. NULL uses every fitted row. A logical vector selects positions. An all-negative vector drops those positions from 1 through length(subset) + n.

arguments.name: iden
arguments.text: If TRUE, prompt for a panel and run identify() until the answer is 0.

arguments.name: labels
arguments.text: Labels for identify(). Defaults to the names of the linear predictor.

arguments.name: ret
arguments.text: If TRUE, return glmdiag. Otherwise return nothing.

origin.details: Four panels are drawn with par(mfrow = c(2, 2)). The top left panel plots jackknife residuals against the linear predictor. The top right panel plots normal quantiles against standardized deviance residuals, with a dashed line of slope 1 through the origin. The bottom left panel plots Cook statistics against h/(1-h). A dashed horizontal line at 8/(n - 2p) is drawn when that value lies inside the Cook range, and a dashed vertical line at 2p/(n - 2p) when that value lies inside the range of h/(1-h). The bottom right panel plots the Cook statistics against case number and repeats the horizontal line when it was inside range. The example fits a gamma log model to the leukaemia data.
origin.value: glmdiag if ret is TRUE, otherwise NULL.
origin.example:
library(boot)
data(leuk, package = "MASS")
leuk.mod <- glm(time ~ ag - 1 + log10(wbc), family = Gamma(log), data = leuk)
leuk.diag <- glm.diag(leuk.mod)
glm.diag.plots(leuk.mod, leuk.diag)

translation.description: Draws the four glm.diag.plots panels with Matplotlib for a gaussian or binomial fit.
translation.usage: glm_diag_plots(glmfit, glmdiag=None, subset=None, iden=False, labels=None, ret=False)

arguments.name: glmfit
arguments.text: A fit returned by glm() in this module.

arguments.name: glmdiag
arguments.text: Diagnostics from glm_diag. None calculates them.

arguments.name: subset
arguments.text: 1-based case numbers for the Cook plot. None uses 1 through n. A boolean array selects positions. An all-negative array drops those positions, matching the R subscript.

arguments.name: iden
arguments.text: Interactive identify() is refused. Leave this false.

arguments.name: labels
arguments.text: Accepted for the R argument. Identification is not drawn.

arguments.name: ret
arguments.text: If true, return the diagnostics dict after drawing. Otherwise return None.

translation.details: A 2 by 2 Matplotlib figure is opened. Points are open circles. The top right x values are normal quantiles, placed by R's rank: ties share the average rank, and the fractional part is dropped before indexing qnorm(ppoints(n)). The axis titles are the ones in the R source, including the swapped QQ titles. Dashed reference lines use the same rules: 8/(n - 2p) horizontally and 2p/(n - 2p) vertically, and only when the value sits inside the plotted range. The manual example is a gamma model of the leukaemia data. This module fits gaussian and binomial models, so the example below is the mammals gaussian fit from cv.glm.
translation.value: The diagnostics dict if ret is true, otherwise None. The figure is left as the current Matplotlib figure.
